requirements.statement: For each required field with aria-invalid="true", the error message stating that the input is invalid is visible and placed in the field's label or in the passage of text associated with it.

rationale.text: Fields with aria-invalid="true" are found in the markup, but the test applies only to those that are required, and a field can be required without a required or aria-required attribute, so the set of fields is a reading of the form. Whether the label or associated passage of such a field holds a visible error message stating that the input is invalid is judgment: code cannot tell an error message from other text in a label or description. A field with aria-invalid="true", a required attribute, and no label or associated passage at all would fail both routes; it is rare, and the entry does not register a check for it. It could support a fail_only claim later, with a check that also rules out labels given by text that is not associated with the field. So the entry is none with no link. No axe-core rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment, because whether a field is required is. Needs is state: aria-invalid is set and error messages are shown after an attempt to validate, so the page as loaded usually holds neither.
